links.outcome: Fairness gaps by race and sex over time with and without population-level model updating
links.effect: Updating restored fairness gaps in some cases (readmission sex gaps) and exacerbated or did not close them in others (pneumonia race gap not closed; ICI gap larger for males); overall performance affected more than fairness.
links.quote: During periods of fairness drift, updating models restored fairness in some cases and exacerbated fairness gaps in others.

links.outcome: Emergence of subgroup performance disparities over time after deployment (fairness drift)
links.effect: Fairness drift observed by race and sex; pneumonia model race accuracy and specificity gaps grew (P<.01 for trend); sex accuracy and specificity gaps increased in original models for all 3 outcomes (P<.01).
links.quote: We observed fairness drift in both the original and temporally updated models.

links.outcome: Performance and calibration drift of deployed prediction models over 10 years
links.effect: Accuracy and calibration deteriorated over time in all models, largest for readmission; surveillance-based updating stabilized calibration for mortality and pneumonia but did not restore accuracy.
links.quote: Accuracy and calibration deteriorated over time in all models, with the largest population-level performance changes observed for the readmission model.

links.outcome: Effect of recalibration triggered by drift detection on overall performance and fairness
links.effect: Updating restored readmission accuracy and calibration but not mortality/pneumonia accuracy; reduced readmission sensitivity below initial; effects on fairness gaps varied.
links.quote: For the readmission model, the surveillance-based model updating process restored both accuracy and calibration to levels comparable or better than initial performance.

links.outcome: Subgroup performance gaps at initial validation by race and sex
links.effect: Specificity and accuracy higher for female vs male in all models; sensitivity lower for female in readmission and pneumonia models; no AUC, O:E, or ICI differences by race or sex.
links.quote: Sensitivity was lower for female vs male patients in models for readmission and pneumonia.

links.outcome: Subgroup accuracy and specificity gaps over time
links.effect: Over 10 years, accuracy and specificity gaps between female and male patients increased across all 3 models (P < .01), and Black-White accuracy and specificity gaps widened for pneumonia (P < .01).
links.quote: Over time, the accuracy and specificity gaps between female and male patients increased in the original models for all 3 outcomes ( P < .01 for trends in gap in both metrics).

links.outcome: Calibration and accuracy after surveillance-based model updating
links.effect: Surveillance-based updating stabilized calibration for mortality and pneumonia but did not restore accuracy, while restoring both calibration and accuracy for readmission; effects on fairness gaps were mixed across outcomes.
